conditioned_scope_clause.text: Documentation of the system architecture for the Tested code

requirements.title: Document Threat Models
requirements.normative_text: Document Threat Models Documented Threat Models for the Tested code MUST be provided, describing each threat, security assumptions, expected responses, and expected outcomes.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: Documented Threat Models for the Tested code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: Documented Threat Models for the Tested code

requirements.title: Annotate Code with NatSpec
requirements.normative_text: Annotate Code with NatSpec All Public Interfaces contained in the Tested code MUST be annotated with inline comments according to the [NatSpec] format that explain the intent behind each function, parameter, event, and return variable, along with developer notes for safe usage.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: All Public Interfaces contained in the Tested code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: All Public Interfaces contained in the Tested code

requirements.title: Implement as Documented
requirements.normative_text: Implement as Documented The Tested code MUST behave as described in the documentation provided for [Q] Document Contract Logic, and [Q] Document System Architecture.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: The Tested code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested code

requirements.title: Enforce Least Privilege
requirements.normative_text: Enforce Least Privilege Tested code that enables privileged access MUST implement appropriate access control mechanisms that provide the least privilege necessary for those interactions, based on the documentation provided for [Q] Document Contract Logic. This is an Overriding Requirement for [M] Protect Self-destruction.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: Tested code that enables privileged access
conditioned_scope_clause.text: Tested code that enables privileged access

requirements.title: Use Revocable and Transferable Access Control Permissions
requirements.normative_text: Use Revocable and Transferable Access Control Permissions If the Tested code makes uses of Access Control for privileged actions, it MUST implement a mechanism to revoke and transfer those permissions.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: If the Tested code makes uses of Access Control for privileged actions, it
conditioned_scope_clause.text: If the Tested code makes uses of Access Control for privileged actions, it

requirements.title: No Single Admin EOA for Privileged Actions
requirements.normative_text: No Single Admin EOA for Privileged Actions If the Tested code makes uses of Access Control for privileged actions, it MUST ensure that all critical administrative tasks require multiple signatures to be executed, unless there is a multisg admin that has greater privileges and can revoke permissions in case of a compromised or rogue EOA and reverse any adverse action the EOA has taken.

conditioned_scope_clause.text: If the Tested code makes uses of Access Control for privileged actions, it

requirements.title: Verify External Calls
requirements.normative_text: Verify External Calls Tested Code that contains external calls MUST document the need for them, and MUST protect them in a way that is fully compatible with the claims of the contract author.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: Tested Code that contains external calls
conditioned_scope_clause.text: Tested Code that contains external calls

requirements.title: Verify tx.origin Usage
requirements.normative_text: Verify tx.origin Usage For Tested Code that uses tx.origin, each instance MUST be consistent with the stated security and functionality objectives of the Tested Code, and MUST NOT allow assertions about contract functionality made for [Q] Document Contract Logic or [Q] Document System Architecture to be violated by another contract, even where that contract is called by a user authorized to interact directly with the Tested Code.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: For Tested Code that uses tx.origin, each instance
conditioned_scope_clause.text: For Tested Code that uses tx.origin, each instance

requirements.title: Specify Solidity Compiler Versions to Produce Consistent Output
requirements.normative_text: Specify Solidity Compiler Versions to Produce Consistent Output The Tested Code MUST specify a range of Solidity versions in its pragma directive(s) that produce the same Bytecode given the same compilation options.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: The Tested Code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Check For and Address New Security Bugs
requirements.normative_text: Check For and Address New Security Bugs Check [solidity-bugs-json] and other sources for bugs announced after 1 November 2023 and address them. This version of the specification was finalized late in 2023. New vulnerabilities are discovered from time to time, on an unpredictable schedule. The latest solidity compiler bug accounted for in this version is SOL-2023-3. Checking for security alerts published too late to be incorporated into the current version of this document is an important technique for maintaining the highest possible security. There are other sources of information on new security vulnerabilities, from [CWE] to following the blogs of many security-oriented organizations such as those that contributed to this specification.

requirements.title: Meet as Many Requirements as Possible
requirements.normative_text: Meet as Many Requirements as Possible The Tested Code SHOULD meet as many requirements of this specification as possible at Security Levels above the Security Level for which it is certified.

conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Use Latest Compiler
requirements.normative_text: Use Latest Compiler The Tested Code SHOULD use the latest available stable Solidity compiler version.

conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Write Clear, Legible Solidity Code
requirements.normative_text: Write Clear, Legible Solidity Code The Tested Code SHOULD be written for easy understanding.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: The Tested Code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Follow Accepted ERC Standards
requirements.normative_text: Follow Accepted ERC Standards The Tested Code SHOULD conform to finalized [ERC] standards when it is reasonably capable of doing so for its use-case.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: The Tested Code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Define a Software License
requirements.normative_text: Define a Software License The Tested Code SHOULD define a software license

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: The Tested Code
conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Disclose New Vulnerabilities Responsibly
requirements.normative_text: Disclose New Vulnerabilities Responsibly Security vulnerabilities that are not addressed by this specification SHOULD be brought to the attention of the Working Group and others through responsible disclosure as described in § 1.4 Feedback and new vulnerabilities.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: Security vulnerabilities that are not addressed by this specification
conditioned_scope_clause.text: Security vulnerabilities that are not addressed by this specification

requirements.title: Use Fuzzing
requirements.normative_text: Use Fuzzing Fuzzing SHOULD be used to probe Tested Code for errors.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: Fuzzing
conditioned_scope_clause.text: Fuzzing

requirements.title: Use Mutation Testing
requirements.normative_text: Use Mutation Testing Mutation Testing SHOULD be used to evaluate and improve the quality of test suites for smart contracts.

conditioned_scope_clause.raw_html: Mutation Testing
conditioned_scope_clause.text: Mutation Testing

requirements.title: Use Formal Verification
requirements.normative_text: Use Formal Verification The Tested Code SHOULD undergo formal verification.

conditioned_scope_clause.text: The Tested Code

requirements.title: Select an Appropriate Threshold for Multisig Wallets
requirements.normative_text: Select an Appropriate Threshold for Multisig Wallets Multisignature requirements for privileged actions SHOULD have a sufficient number of signers, and NOT require "1 of N" nor all signatures.
